statement: The CI file this component emits MUST take, from the component's declaration and never from the service declaration, exactly one trusted signer and one pinned shared-pipeline reference for the provider the service's delivery stanza names.

title: Every STEGO check runs before release
statement: The pipeline this component emits MUST run drift, vet, test, a reproducible build and the executable match on every provider, and MUST NOT release an image for delivery when any of them fails.

title: Build and signing are separate jobs
statement: The pipeline this component emits MUST build in a job with read permission and no signing credential, and MUST sign in a separate job that fetches the build's artifact by its immutable ID and signs only after the digests match the build job's outputs.

title: The signer runs pinned verification code the caller cannot choose
statement: The signing job this component emits MUST run the STEGO verification code pinned in the registry, and MUST NOT run code, a pipeline definition or a reference that the calling service's source selects.

title: The pipeline carries the delivery policy the gate enforces
statement: The pipeline this component emits MUST carry the delivery policy file that the platform's gate, Konflux Enterprise Contract, enforces, derived from the service declaration and the registry's advisories, and the delivery check MUST evaluate the same policy, so that the gate and the check refuse the same image.

title: A namespace comes only from a declared profile
statement: The allocator this component emits MUST create a namespace only for a profile the declaration names, with that profile's prefix, quota, accounts, bindings and network rules, and MUST take from its caller only the profile name, the namespace name and the owner, never a permission or a rule.

title: Every allocated namespace is owned and marked
statement: Each namespace the allocator writes MUST carry its owner and the allocator's installation marker, and the allocator MUST refuse every write, deletion included, to a namespace whose owner differs; a namespace of the same name under another owner is an error, never evidence.

title: An allocation is pending until it is complete
statement: The allocator MUST report an allocation as pending, not done, while its namespace, a binding or a peer allocation it depends on is absent or being deleted, and MUST let a worker check an allocation's identity without changing it.

title: Identity is sealed once
statement: Identity labels and annotations the allocator copies from the consumer's immutable record MUST be set once on the namespace, and a later value that differs MUST be an error, never an overwrite.

title: Allocated accounts mount no token and belong to one owner
statement: Every ServiceAccount the allocator creates in an allocated namespace MUST set automountServiceAccountToken false, and its name MUST derive from the owner so that two owners never share one account.

title: Release is complete and owner-checked
statement: Release MUST remove the cluster role bindings first and report pending until each is gone, then delete the namespace only as its owner; cleanup counts as complete only when the namespace is gone, never because a namespace of that name exists under another owner.

title: The allocator's power derives from the profiles
statement: The permissions of the allocator worker MUST derive from the declared roles and profiles only, and the component MUST refuse a declaration that adds Kubernetes permissions to that worker or names an allocator without profiles.

title: A declaration stays reviewable
statement: The component MUST refuse a declaration with more than sixteen roles, more than sixteen profiles, more than sixteen Pod rules in one profile, or a rule beyond its size bounds, so that the emitted policy can be read in full.

title: A match condition reads the request only
statement: A match condition in a policy this component emits MUST read only request fields, never the namespace object or a composed variable; checks of namespace labels, profile, owner, account and caller MUST run in validation expressions, where missing namespace data denies the request; and a policy for one allocator MUST NOT select another allocator's namespaces.

title: Control account names are reserved to the installer
statement: The control-account guard MUST deny the creation of a ServiceAccount whose name or generateName prefix is the allocator's name or a declared control-worker name unless the caller holds the installation capability for that installation path, also in a profile with no managed workload account; it MUST NOT select an unreserved name or an update to an existing account; and the capability for one installation MUST NOT admit the names of another.

title: A peer binding is declared whole
statement: The component MUST refuse a peer binding whose subject profile is its own destination, whose owner label or suffix length differs from the destination's, that names no managed account or not the named alias, or that grants a cluster-scoped role.

title: A peer grant is checked against a sealed source
statement: The allocator MUST create the destination's limits and accounts before it reads any related source; MUST record each imported subject account name in the destination's sealed annotations and create no such account locally; MUST stop the grant, not report pending, when the source has a foreign owner, a changed identity, an automounted token or a denied read; and the admission policy MUST deny a grant whose role, subject namespace or subject name differs from the declared role, the derived namespace and the recorded name.

title: Row-level security on every owned table
statement: The migration this component emits MUST set ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every tenant-owned table, with one policy whose USING and WITH CHECK compare the tenant column of ST-SUP-RC01-OC40 with the tenant setting of the transaction.

title: The runtime role owns nothing
statement: The role migration this component emits MUST create a runtime role, an owner role, a worker role <service>_worker and a relay login role <service>_relay, MUST revoke CONNECT, CREATE and TEMPORARY on the service's database from PUBLIC and grant CONNECT only to the owner, runtime, worker and relay roles of the service, so no role of another service in the same cluster can connect to it; because PostgreSQL checks CONNECT only when a session starts, MUST commit that revoke and then refuse to go on while a session of a role that is not a role of the service, nor a superuser, is open in the database, other than its own, with an error that gives the count of such sessions and names no role, and MUST NOT terminate a session; MUST make the NOLOGIN purge role of the service alone, <service role prefix>_idempotency_purge, with NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS and NOINHERIT, when it is missing, MUST make the owner role a member of it WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE and MUST give it no CREATE on the schema public; MUST make the NOLOGIN outbox relay role of the service alone, <service role prefix>_outbox_relay, with NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS and NOINHERIT, when it is missing, MUST make the owner role a member of it WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE and MUST give it no CREATE on the schema public (ST-SUP-RP01-LC19); MUST take a set runtime_role and owner_role only as <prefix>_runtime and <prefix>_owner of one prefix, so every role name of the service is its prefix and a suffix of its own, and MUST refuse a role prefix that ends with the part by which one role suffix is longer than another, such as _outbox for _outbox_relay and _relay, so no role name of one service is a role name of another service in the same cluster (ST-SUP-Q107, option a, decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11); MUST let the owner role grant CREATE on public, so that the idempotency migration can give it to the purge role only while it makes the purge function (ST-SUP-RP07-LC11), and the authorization migration to the outbox relay role only while it makes its state hook functions (ST-SUP-RP06-LC21); MUST revoke from the runtime role every privilege but the ones the emitted statements use, and MUST NOT grant BYPASSRLS or ownership to the runtime role; so the first migration job needs no role or grant that a database administrator makes by hand. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that the role migration makes these roles and grants from the declaration. The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), in the recheck of PR #206 (finding F1). The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), in the narrow recheck of PR #206 (finding H1, option b). The orchestrator decided ST-SUP-Q106 option (a) under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11): the outbox relay role is one role of each service. Before it changes anything, the role migration MUST refuse a role of its names that exists and is not the service's alone: a role that holds a privilege on, or owns, another database on which the owner of the service holds no CREATE; a purge or outbox relay role that can log in; a role that is a member of a role that the migration does not grant it; or a role that has a member, or a holder of ADMIN, that the migration does not grant: the owner in the purge and outbox relay roles, without ADMIN, and in the owner role, without ADMIN, the one migration login that the operator names in the setting stego.migration_login (for example SET stego.migration_login = 'shop_migrator' before the role migration), so a role that a login with CREATEROLE made first, which holds that login as a member with ADMIN, is refused; a member that is a superuser is refused as any other member; the refusal names the role and the sign, and for a member the member (decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, in the delta recheck of PR #213, finding G1) (decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, in the security review of PR #213, finding F1). The role migration MUST also refuse, before it changes anything, a named migration login that has a member or a holder of ADMIN, a superuser included, since each would reach the owner role through the login; the refusal names the login and its members (decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, follow-up L1 of the delta recheck 2 of PR #213). No upgrade path exists from the former cluster role stego_outbox_relay to the outbox relay role of a service: a database whose relay functions belong to it stops the outbox migration; no release of the runtime exists (decided by orchestrator under owner delegation, 2026-11-11, in the security review of PR #213, finding F4). The role migration MUST set the search path of the runtime, worker and relay roles to public, pg_temp, so a name with no schema resolves in pg_catalog, public and the temporary schema of the session only, never in a schema named after the role (ST-STD-TXN-R19). The orchestrator decided the fix of S1 of the recheck of PR #243 on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation.

title: Workers and controllers iterate tenants
statement: A worker or controller this component emits with tenants set to each MUST iterate the tenants and open one transaction per tenant with that tenant set, and MUST NOT open a transaction without a tenant.

title: Shared and system entities stay apart
statement: An entity declared shared MUST be readable by every tenant and writable only by the owner role in the migration job: the runtime role MUST hold SELECT and no other privilege on its table. An entity declared system MUST carry no tenant and MUST NOT be exposed through a tenant request. Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation: with no bypass role (ST-SUP-RT09), the system principal that writes a shared entity is the owner role in the migration job; the runtime role gets SELECT only on a shared table, so no binding, with runs_as tenant or system, writes a shared row.

title: The isolation suite runs as the runtime role
statement: The isolation test suite this component emits MUST run as the runtime role, not as a superuser, and MUST assert that a cross-tenant read returns zero rows and that a cross-tenant insert fails, for every owned table.

title: Provision and Retire are commands decided on the service's resource
statement: The tenancy component MUST emit Provision as POST <base path>/stego/tenants and Retire as POST <base path>/stego/tenants/{tenantId}/retire, each a command that verifies the caller, decides the declared permission on the service-level resource <resource type>:<service name>, such as service:todo-svc, and not on a tenant, through the authorization port at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 before it changes anything, requires an Idempotency-Key, and is in the operation-to-permission table and never public (ST-SUP-RC29-OC15); the operator's principal holds the provision and retire permissions on that resource, so the first tenant of an empty service can be provisioned.

title: A provisioning change and its audit row commit together
statement: Provision and Retire MUST write their audit row through the audit runtime in the transaction that changes the tenant list, with the command name as the action, the caller as the actor and the tenant as the resource, and a denied or failed call MUST write its outcome row in its own short transaction, as ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 states.

title: A claim for a tenant that is not provisioned is refused before any handler
statement: The request path that the tenancy component emits MUST look the claim's tenant up in the tenant list, or in a cache of it no older than 5 s, after verification and before any handler, decision or fill, and MUST refuse a tenant that is absent or retired with 403 and the code tenant.not_provisioned, or with PERMISSION_DENIED and the same code for a gRPC call; the two provisioning routes of ST-SUP-RC27-OC09 are exempt, because they are decided on the service-level resource and not on a tenant.

title: Retire keeps every row and stops the tenant's workers
statement: Retire MUST set the tenant's retire time in the tenant list and MUST delete no row of the tenant; the iterator MUST skip a retired tenant from the next tick (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07), and a consumer handler MUST return a permanent refusal for a message of a retired tenant without calling the fill, so the outbox parks it with an alert (ST-SUP-RP01-LC12).

title: Diff and redaction follow field sensitivity
statement: The per-entity diff and redaction functions this component emits MUST redact every field declared pii in before and after, also when the service's Audit setting says audit.pii keep (ST-DECL-EN10), which keeps the field in the source record only, MUST NOT store a field declared secret, and MUST hash the redacted record, so that an audit row never holds personal data and an erasure changes the source row only, never an audit row.

title: The audit row commits with the change
statement: Each mutation this component emits MUST write its audit row in the same transaction as the change, so a rollback leaves no row and a commit leaves exactly one.

title: A denied or failed mutation is audited apart
statement: A mutation that is denied or fails MUST write an audit row with outcome denied or failed and its error code in a short transaction of its own, after the mutation's transaction rolled back.

title: A read of personal data is audited
statement: For every entity with a field declared pii, the emitted code MUST write an audit row with action read for each single read, and one such row for each resource that a list returns with the field, so a list writes at most one page of rows.

title: A fill's relationship write carries the slot name
statement: A relationship write that a slot fill makes through its authorization handle MUST be audited in the fill's transaction with the slot name as the action and the resource and relation as the resource fields.

title: The audit table is append-only
statement: The migration this component emits MUST create one audit_event table per service partitioned by month, with the tables audit_chain_heads, audit_anchor_boundaries and audit_retention_checkpoints and the function audit_maintain() of ST-SUP-RP05-LC10, each table with row-level security enabled and forced, MUST grant the runtime role SELECT and INSERT only on audit_event with UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked, and MUST add a trigger that rejects UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. Generation MUST refuse a retention of more than 1200 months, from the declaration or the component setting, with an error that names the bound. The orchestrator decided the call by schema, the grants of the function and the bound of the retention on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation, in the security review of PR #239 (L1, L2).

title: Every audit row is copied to the sink
statement: The outbox binding this component emits MUST enqueue each audit row to the audit-sink port in the audit row's transaction, keyed by the audit event id, and the component MUST require the audit-sink port and provide no port.

title: The anchor job is scheduled
statement: The job schedule this component emits MUST register the anchor job that publishes, for each tenant's chain, the latest hash and the row count to the audit sink at the anchor period that this component's own declaration in the registry sets, and the maintenance loop of ST-SUP-RP05-LC10, so a truncation is detected outside the service.

title: The entity history query reads the local table
statement: The entity history query this component emits MUST read the local audit_event table by tenant, resource type and resource id, ordered by occurred_at, and MUST return the redacted before, after and patch only.

title: Every operation maps to one permission
statement: The operation-to-permission table this component emits MUST map each declared operation of a protected entity to one permission of the entity's resource type, and the generator MUST refuse an operation whose permission the compiled schema does not declare; the create of an entity with no parent MUST be decided on the service-level resource <resource type>:<service name> of ST-SUP-RC27-OC09, so its permission is one that the compiled schema declares on that resource type (the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11).

title: Evaluate runs before the operation and the slot chain
statement: The emitted handler MUST call Evaluate with the subject, the permission and the resource before each operation and before the slot chain, at consistency at least as fresh as the row's authz_token or the service's revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), whichever is fresher, and MUST treat a deny as a decision answered with 404, the same answer as a missing row (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06), never as an error. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that a write to a missing or a denied row is answered 404, the same as a read (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06): one rule for every operation.

title: The tenant predicate comes before the authorization filter
statement: The emitted list and read code MUST apply the tenant predicate before any authorization filter, and MUST NOT let a permission widen a tenant.

title: A list is filtered by its declared cardinality
statement: For a collection declared with small expected cardinality the emitted list MUST filter with a resource search; otherwise it MUST page the database and call a batch evaluation per page; the search and every batch call MUST run at least as fresh as the service's revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13) read at the time of that call, and a later search page MUST keep the first page's consistency in its page token and be filtered at the current floor as ST-SUP-RP06-LC05 states; and an empty result MUST be 200 with an empty list.

title: The declared tuples of a row are enqueued in the row's transaction
statement: The declared relationships of each protected entity (ST-DECL-UC06-R04), with the relation of each reference of the row to an entity with a resource type (ST-DECL-EN02), as the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11, MUST become tuples on create, update and delete, MUST be enqueued to the authz destination in the same transaction as the row, and every tuple MUST join the transaction's revocation (ST-SUP-RP06-LC12). This component emits no relationship mapper: the command generator gives each entity its Relationships list, and the command runtime writes the tuples (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05), as the orchestrator decided under the Product owner's delegation on 2026-11-13 (ST-SUP-Q118, option a).

title: The relay token is stored on the row
statement: The migration this component emits MUST add an authz_token column to every protected entity's table and MUST create the table authz_floor with one row, with no tenant_id and no row-level security because it holds no tenant data, which the runtime role may read and only the relay may update; and the destination handler MUST store the token the provider returned on the owning row.

title: The authz destination handler is idempotent and ordered
statement: The outbox destination handler this component emits MUST write tuples with touch and delete only, in order per resource key, MUST park a poisoned entry and alert without blocking other keys, and MUST be safe to run twice.

title: No handler and no fill writes a tuple directly
statement: The emitted code MUST NOT call the authz-relationships port from a handler or a fill, and a fill MUST NOT receive a provider client; every tuple reaches the provider through the outbox relay.

title: The slot handle carries the tenant, the subject and the decision
statement: The slot contract this component emits MUST pass the fill the tenant, the subject and an authz handle whose Evaluate decides at the consistency floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, the fresher of the row token and the service's revocation floor, so a fill decides with the same floor as the handler.

title: Relate and Unrelate go through the outbox
statement: The authz handle's Relate and Unrelate MUST enqueue the tuple in the current transaction's outbox for the relay, and MUST NOT write to the provider.

title: The handle exposes only the declared relations
statement: The authz handle MUST expose only the relations the slot binding declares under Relationships written, as resource_type#relation, and the generator MUST refuse a declared relation that the compiled schema does not hold.

title: System principals are subjects
statement: The relay and each controller the emitted code runs MUST call the port with their own service_account subject, and the generator MUST refuse a slot or a declaration that names a bypass flag.

title: The schema compiles at checking
statement: The generator MUST compile the declared schema at checking and refuse a resource type, permission, relation or caveat parameter that an entity, collection or slot names and the schema does not declare, and MUST NOT write the schema to the provider at generation.

title: One allow and one deny per permission
statement: The conformance tests this component emits MUST load the declared schema into an embedded SpiceDB and assert one allow and one deny for every permission the operation table names.

title: No route without a decision
statement: The emitted router MUST register a route only from the operation-to-permission table, MUST emit for an operation declared public an explicit allow whose audit action carries the reason, and MUST NOT hold a default or a fallback that answers a route the table lacks; a route without a decision cannot exist in the emitted code.

title: A mutation that writes a tuple answers pending with its revocation
statement: The emitted handler of an operation whose transaction enqueues a tuple, touch or delete, MUST answer with the header Authz-Revocation: pending and the header Authz-Revocation-Location with the path of the revocation status route for the transaction's revocation, both set before the commit, so the idempotency record stores them and a replay stays byte for byte; an operation that enqueues no tuple MUST send neither header.

title: The revocation status route answers the state of a revocation
statement: The component MUST emit a revocation status route that reads one revocation by its identity through Status and MUST answer 200 with the state pending, complete, parked, or failed, and no token of the provider (ST-SUP-RP10-LC35, security review of #286).

title: The revocation status route has its own decision
statement: The operation-to-permission table MUST hold the revocation status route with its own decision, which allows only the principal and tenant that made the write and calls no provider, the route MUST answer 404 to any other caller as for an identity that does not exist, the router MUST register the route only from that entry, and the route MUST NOT be public.

title: The status route waits within bounds and holds no connection
statement: The revocation status route MUST honor Prefer: wait=N (RFC 7240) by waiting at most N seconds and at most the wait cap, the setting wait_cap whose default is 10 seconds and which the generator MUST refuse when it is not above zero or is above 25 seconds, below the write timeout of 30 seconds of the generated HTTP server, so a full wait leaves time to write its answer, and MUST answer at once when the state is no longer pending; it MUST send Preference-Applied with the seconds it allowed, which is the cap when the cap cut the wait; it MUST NOT hold a database transaction or a pooled connection while it waits; and it MUST hold at most the waiter limit, the setting waiter_limit whose default is 100, and at most the waiter limit of a tenant, the setting tenant_waiter_limit whose default is 10, of the waits of one tenant, and answer a request over a limit at once without waiting (ST-SUP-RP06-LC24).

title: The schema declares the outbox resolve permission
statement: When the service binds durable-events, the generator MUST refuse at checking a schema that does not declare the resource type outbox_destination with the permission resolve, and the emitted code MUST build the outbox worker with the authz decision port, so Resolve decides that permission like any other check.

title: A slot fill gets its binding's probe from the context
statement: The slot adapter this component emits MUST pass each bound slot fill a context that holds the probe of its slot binding, bound to the call's span context, tenant, principal and binding name, which the fill reads through the binding's generated accessor (ST-SUP-RC34-OC04), as ST-SUP-RC20-OC36 states for the rest-api slots, and MUST NOT put the probe on the slot handle.

title: Emitted tuples and checks use tenant-qualified resource IDs
statement: The relationship mappers, handlers and adapters this component emits MUST build every resource ID they pass the authorization runtime from the row's tenant and key in the form that ST-SUP-RP06-LC22 states, through the runtime's own function, and MUST NOT format a resource ID themselves. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-08); review of PR #154.

title: The migration job writes the schema before the service starts
statement: The generated migration job MUST write the emitted schema, with the floor marker definition, to SpiceDB through WriteSchema before the service starts, so the schema is versioned with the release; and it MUST refuse, writing nothing, when SpiceDB holds a schema that the new one would break: a removed definition or relation that has relationships. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator, who decided it on 2026-11-10 in the review of PR #181 (ST-SUP-Q68).

title: The key header is on the POST and PATCH operations only
statement: The OpenAPI document this component emits MUST carry the Idempotency-Key header parameter only on the operations that take it, the POST and PATCH operations, required on create and accepted on patch, with 400, 409 and 422 problem responses, MUST carry no Idempotency-Key parameter on get, put and delete, and the service MUST ignore the header on get, put and delete.

title: Problem types sit under the service base
statement: The problem type URIs this component emits MUST sit under the service's declared problem base and MUST name idempotency-key-missing, idempotency-key-in-progress and idempotency-key-reused.

title: The fingerprint is per operation
statement: The fingerprint this component emits MUST be the runtime's field fingerprint (ST-SUP-RP07-LC10) with the list of the fields the operation takes; the component MUST emit only that list for each operation, and no decode or hash code of its own. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: The key row commits with the write
statement: The idempotency wrapper MUST claim the key row, run the handler and complete the row inside the command's one transaction, through command.Run (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11), scoped by tenant, principal and key, so a crash before commit leaves no key and no write. A collection create or patch is a generated command (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37), so it takes the same path. This answers ST-SUP-Q66 with option B. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: A failed response is not stored
statement: The wrapper call MUST NOT keep a key row for a response with status 5xx, 429 or 503; the row MUST roll back with the write.

title: The conformance tests cover replay, reuse, race and crash
statement: The conformance tests this component emits MUST replay the same body and get the stored response with Idempotent-Replayed true, send a different body and get 422, send the same key twice at once and get 409, and crash before commit and find nothing stored.

title: The purge job is the runtime's
statement: The component MUST register the runtime's purge job (ST-SUP-RP07-LC09) with the declared retention, and MUST emit no purge loop of its own. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: Four shared tables with declared codes as constraints
statement: The migration this component emits MUST create one set of the tables accounts, transfers, entries and balance_snapshots that every declared ledger shares, with each row keyed by ledger_id, and with the declared transfer codes and account limits as CHECK constraints.

title: Money is integer minor units with one currency
statement: Every money column this component emits MUST be amount bigint with currency char(3), each ledger MUST hold one currency, and the generator MUST refuse a float money field.

title: A transfer posts through the runtime ledger
statement: The ledger port this component emits MUST post every transfer through the runtime ledger (ST-SUP-RP08-LC03), and the generator MUST emit no posting SQL and no post_transfer function of its own, because the posting code is the same for every declaration (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05).

title: Post and void are new rows
statement: A pending transfer MUST be posted or voided by a new transfer row that carries pending_id, once only, and the emitted code MUST NOT change a transfer's amount or entries in place.

title: A correction is a reversal
statement: A reversal MUST be a new transfer that carries reverses, the original MUST get reversed_by, and the emitted code MUST refuse a second reversal of one transfer.

title: Transfers replay by idempotency key
statement: The transfers table MUST carry UNIQUE on ledger_id and idempotency_key, and the insert MUST use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING so a retry returns the original row.

title: Only a limited account locks
statement: A post MUST lock the account row FOR UPDATE only for an account declared with min_balance, and MUST NOT lock an account declared hot or without a limit.

title: The ledger tables are append-only
statement: The migration this component emits MUST apply the runtime ledger's DDL text (ST-SUP-RP08-LC09): SELECT only for the runtime role on the ledger tables, EXECUTE on the owner functions, the guard triggers, and ownership left to the owner role.

title: Endpoints follow the declared operations
statement: The REST endpoints this component emits MUST exist only for the declared operations among create, post, void, reverse, read and list, and the generator MUST refuse update or delete on a ledger collection.

title: OpenAPI carries integer amounts and string currencies
statement: The OpenAPI schema this component emits MUST type amount as integer and currency as string, and MUST NOT emit a number type for money.

title: The ledger port has seven operations
statement: The ledger port this component emits MUST offer seven operations: post, pend, post a pending transfer, void, reverse, balance, and balance at an effective time; and a slot fill MUST post only through it.

title: The snapshot and check jobs run in controller mode
statement: The job registration this component emits MUST register the balance snapshot job and the ledger_check job in controller mode, and a failed check MUST be a health signal.

title: The command slot takes the request and the handle only
statement: The command slot this component emits MUST give the fill the command's decoded request and one command handle, and nothing else that reaches storage, authorization, audit, the outbox or the network.

title: Each declared command gets one handler that calls its one fill
statement: The generator MUST emit one handler per command the declaration declares, bound to the one fill the command names, and MUST refuse a command whose fill does not implement the command slot, naming the command and the fill.

title: A command fill's whole import closure is checked
statement: Generation MUST refuse a command fill whose import closure, as go list -deps reports it, breaks the import rule of ST-EXT-UC01-R03, and MUST name the fill, the refused package and the import chain that reaches it. The check MUST run in internal/fill behind the compiler's FillQualifier port, not in a generator, because a generator does no file or process access. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: The handler verifies, opens one transaction and sets the tenant before the fill
statement: The handler this component emits MUST verify the identity, take the tenant from the verified claim and open one store transaction with that tenant set before it calls the fill, and MUST call the fill at most once per transaction.

title: The fill's writes commit together or not at all
statement: The handler MUST commit the transaction only when the fill returns no error, and MUST roll back every write, audit row, staged effect and key row of the transaction when the fill returns an error or panics.

title: The command's permission is decided before the fill
statement: The handler MUST evaluate the command's declared permission for the principal through the authorization port before it calls the fill, on the resource whose ID the command's resource member gives, and, for a command that creates or moves a row, the permission that the declaration names for each set reference on the referenced row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC05), at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, and MUST answer a deny as a decision with 404, the same answer as a missing row, without calling the fill. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that a write to a missing or a denied row is answered 404, the same as a read (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06): one rule for every operation.

title: A command leaves audit rows with its name and outcome
statement: A command MUST leave one audit row with the outcome ok for each write of a committed command, with the command name as the action and the principal as the actor, in the command's transaction (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06), and the handler MUST write one audit row with the command name as the action in its own short transaction with the outcome denied or failed when the command is denied or fails. The outcome MUST be one of ok, denied and failed (ST-SUP-RP05-LC01): a conflict is failed with the error_code conflict (ST-SUP-RC32-OC10), and a COMMIT whose outcome is not known is failed with the fixed error_code commit_outcome_unknown (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25); when that commit took effect, the ok rows of its writes stay beside it. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that a committed command leaves one ok row per write, with the command as the action, and no row for the command itself.

title: A command runs once per idempotency key
statement: The handler MUST require an Idempotency-Key on every command and answer a request without one with 400 as ST-SUP-RP07-LC04 states, and MUST run each command inside the idempotency wrapper keyed by it, so a retry with the same key and body replays the stored response and does not call the fill again.

title: A command fill's error leaves only as a fixed code
statement: The generator MUST emit one typed refusal value for each refusal that the command declares (ST-DECL-EN18, ST-DECL-EN19), and the handler MUST answer a fill that returns one with its declared status and code, a conflict as ST-SUP-RC32-OC10 states, and any other error with 500 and the code internal; it MUST NOT put the error's text, or a value it wraps, in the response, in the audit row's error_code or in the completion log of ST-SUP-RP03-LC12, as ST-SUP-RC10-OC17 states for the application's domain errors.

title: A conflict is answered 409 with the code conflict
statement: The generator MUST pass each command's declared Retry on conflict (ST-DECL-EN18) to Run, and the handler MUST answer a conflict that Run returns after its last attempt (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) with 409 and the fixed code conflict on the HTTP route and with the status ABORTED on a gRPC method, MUST write its audit row with the outcome failed and the error_code conflict in its own short transaction, as ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 states for a failed command, MUST store no response under the idempotency key, so a retry with the same key runs the command again, and MUST NOT put a version or a value of the row in the response.

title: A command has one protobuf request and response pair
statement: The generator MUST emit one protobuf request message and one response message for each command, used by both the HTTP route (JSON through protojson) and the gRPC method, and the fill MUST take the decoded request message. This answers ST-SUP-Q61 with option A. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: Each effect destination keeps its declared delivery properties
statement: The destinations setting of a component MUST declare must_land and idempotent for each destination, and generation MUST refuse a destination that leaves either out; the generator MUST give each effect destination of a command to the runtime with the must_land and idempotent that its destination declares, and MUST give the command's declared effect names to its CommandSpec (ST-SUP-RP10-LC07). The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: The contract gives typed helpers for each declared relation
statement: For each relation resource_type#relation that a command declares in relationships_written, the command contract package MUST give the two helpers <Command>Relate<Relation> and <Command>Unrelate<Relation>, which take the command handle, a loaded value of the written entity of that resource type and the subject type and identity, build the tenant-qualified tuple of the row (ST-SUP-RC29-OC22) and call Relate or Unrelate of the handle, so a fill never builds a resource identity and cannot name a relation that the command does not declare; the generator MUST refuse a declared relation of a resource type that the command writes no entity of, and a relation that the runtime writes alone for a written entity of that resource type: the relation of a declared relationship, of the subject source field or caller, or of a reference (ST-SUP-Q118).

title: The query slot takes the request and the handle only
statement: The query slot this component emits MUST give the fill the query's decoded request and one query handle, and nothing else that reaches storage, authorization, the outbox or the network.

title: Each declared query gets one handler that calls its one fill
statement: The generator MUST emit one handler per query the declaration declares, bound to the one fill the query names, and MUST refuse a query whose fill does not implement the query slot, naming the query and the fill.

title: A query fill's whole import closure is checked
statement: Generation MUST refuse a query fill whose import closure, as go list -deps reports it, breaks the import rule of ST-EXT-UC01-R03, and MUST name the fill, the refused package and the import chain that reaches it.

title: The handler verifies and opens one read-only tenant transaction before the fill
statement: The handler this component emits MUST verify the identity, take the tenant from the verified claim and open one READ ONLY store transaction with that tenant set before it calls the fill, and MUST call the fill at most once per request.

title: The query's permission is decided before the fill
statement: For a query that names a resource member, the handler MUST evaluate the query's declared permission on that resource at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 before it calls the fill and MUST answer a deny with 404, the same answer as a missing row (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06, ST-SUP-RP11-LC17), without calling the fill; the fill's repositories keep the read permission of the entity (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06), so a query whose permission is not that read permission decides only its own permission on the requested row; for a list query, which names none, the handler MUST NOT decide before the fill, and every row the fill reads MUST be decided on the query's declared permission at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 and filtered as ST-SUP-RP11-LC07 states. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that a denied get query is answered 404 and that a fill keeps the read permission of the entity.

title: A query changes nothing
statement: A query the handler serves MUST leave every entity, outbox and idempotency table as it found it, except the audit rows of a read of personal data and their outbox entries for the audit sink (ST-SUP-RP05-LC07).

title: A query fill's error leaves only as a fixed code
statement: The generator MUST emit one typed refusal value for each refusal that the query declares (ST-DECL-EN18, ST-DECL-EN19), and the handler MUST answer a fill that returns one with its declared status and code, and any other error with 500 and the code internal; it MUST NOT put the error's text, or a value it wraps, in the response, in the audit row's error_code or in the completion log of ST-SUP-RP03-LC12, as ST-SUP-RC10-OC17 states for the application's domain errors. On the runtime data path the generated code MUST set the refusal lookup of query.HTTP to queries.Declared (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17); the Product owner decided on 2026-11-11.

title: A stream query is served over gRPC only
statement: A query whose Method is a server stream (ST-DECL-INV73) MUST be served over gRPC only: the compiler MUST mark the query as a stream from the proto files that the grpc-application component declares, the grpc-application component MUST call the generated Stream function on query.RunStream (ST-SUP-RP11-LC13), and the generator MUST emit no HTTP route for it. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11; an HTTP stream waits until an HTTP client needs one.

title: An entity of small expected cardinality lists through the resource search
statement: The query entity that this component emits, for its own queries and for the views that the rest-api component takes (query.ViewFile), MUST set Search for an entity whose expected cardinality is small (ST-DECL-EN02), so the runtime lists it through the provider's resource search (ST-SUP-RP11-LC20); MUST NOT set it for an entity of large or no expected cardinality; and generation MUST refuse another value, and a small entity with no resource type. The orchestrator decided ST-SUP-Q111 option (c) on 2026-11-12 under the Product owner's delegation.

title: One typed method per observation
statement: The generator MUST emit, for each observation that the declaration declares, one exported method named in Go mixed case from the observation name, whose parameters are first one loaded value of each entity that a field reads, in the order the fields first name them, as a generated type that only a read or a write through the fill's handle can make, and then the enum, bool and measure fields in order with their Go types and, for a histogram, the value last as float64. The method MUST read each entity field from the loaded value itself, and MUST have no context, message, format, error, string or variadic parameter and no result.

title: An enum field is a closed type
statement: For each enum field the generator MUST emit a named type with one constant for each declared value, and the probe method MUST take that type, so a fill cannot pass a value that the declaration does not declare. The type is a named string type with one constant per value: Go lets an untyped string constant convert to it, so the closed set holds for every typed value, and the runtime drops and counts a value outside the set. This answers ST-SUP-Q62 with option a. The owner delegated this decision to the orchestrator (2026-11-09).

title: Each emitter gets a probe with its own observations only
statement: The generator MUST emit one probe type for each command, query, worker, process method and slot binding of the declaration, with the methods of the observations that name it in Emitted by and no other method, and MUST bind each probe to the call's span context, tenant, principal and emitter name through the probe runtime (ST-SUP-RP12-LC02).

title: Each fill gets its probe through its input
statement: The generated handler of each command and query, and the generated runner of each worker, MUST give its fill the bound probe through the command or query handle (ST-SUP-RP10-LC14, ST-SUP-RP11-LC11). For each other slot binding, the slot's component MUST put the binding's bound probe in the context it passes the fill (ST-SUP-RC20-OC36, ST-SUP-RC29-OC21), and the fill MUST read it only through the binding's generated accessor; the probe is on no slot handle and in no protobuf message. A fill MUST NOT get the probe of another emitter: the accessor of a binding MUST return, in the context of another binding, a probe that emits nothing and counts the attempt. A slot input MUST NOT hold a writer or a logger.

title: A probe method fans out through the probe runtime only
statement: Each generated probe method MUST call the probe runtime (ST-SUP-RP12) with its observation's descriptor and its typed values only, and MUST NOT write to a writer, a logger or an OpenTelemetry API itself.

title: A recorder probe is emitted for fill tests
statement: The generator MUST emit, for each probe type, a constructor for tests that binds the probe to a probe.Recorder with a fixed tenant, principal and emitter name and gives the test a way to end the call with a commit or a rollback, so a fill test can call its fill with that probe and assert its emissions (ST-SUP-RP12-LC10, ST-SUP-RP12-LC11).

title: The observation catalog is emitted
statement: The generator MUST emit the file observations.json, which lists each declared observation in name order with its signal name domain.<name>, its kind, severity, fields with their types, value and unit, emitters and outcome measured, so a service's own business outcome measure can name the signal that it counts, and the same declaration MUST give the same bytes.

title: A slot fill gets loaded values from the validated request
statement: For each slot binding whose probe has a method that reads an entity field, the generated code MUST make the loaded value of that entity from the request entity after the request is validated, and MUST give it to the fill through the binding's accessor beside the probe; the fill MUST NOT be able to make a loaded value from a value it builds itself.

title: The worker slot takes its input and the handle only
statement: The worker slot this component emits MUST give a fill of a worker with an every trigger the tick time and one command handle that RunWorker binds, and a fill of a worker with a consumes trigger the decoded message, its effect name and one command handle that RunConsumer binds (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16), and nothing else that reaches storage, authorization, audit, the outbox or the network.

title: Each declared worker gets one runner that calls its one fill
statement: The generator MUST emit one runner for each worker that the declaration declares, bound to the one fill that the worker names, and MUST refuse a worker whose fill does not implement the worker slot of its trigger, naming the worker and the fill.

title: A worker fill is checked as every fill is
statement: Generation MUST refuse a worker fill whose import closure, as go list -deps reports it, breaks the import rule of ST-EXT-UC01-R03, or whose packages break ST-EXT-UC01-R05 or ST-EXT-UC01-R07, naming the fill, the refused package or call and the chain that reaches it, and MUST wire a worker fill only when it is qualified and fits its binding (ST-GEN-INV10).

title: An interval worker runs each tenant once a tick, and ticks do not overlap
statement: The runner of a worker with an every trigger MUST run only in the worker mode (ST-SUP-RP09-LC01), MUST start a tick at each multiple of the interval since the Unix epoch, so every replica schedules the same ticks (ST-SUP-RP10-LC21), MUST run RunWorker at most once for each tenant of the tick through the tenant runtime's iterator, one transaction for each tenant (ST-SUP-RP04-LC05), MUST NOT start a tick while the previous one runs, and MUST skip a tick that comes while one runs, never queue it, and count it as the built-in counter worker.tick.skipped (ST-SUP-RP12-LC21).

title: A single worker runs only while it holds its lease
statement: The runner of a single worker MUST acquire and renew the lease stego.worker.<worker name> through the lease runtime with the declared lease TTL and a renew interval of two thirds of it, as the lease runtime's defaults of 15 s and 10 s are (ST-SUP-RP09-LC02), MUST start a tick only while it holds the lease, MUST pass the held lease to RunWorker (ST-SUP-RP10-LC20, ST-SUP-RP10-LC22), and MUST cancel the running tick and start none when it loses the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC04).

title: A consuming worker is the one handler of its destination
statement: For a worker with a consumes trigger the generated code MUST register one destination handler on the service's outbox with the consumed destination name, as idempotent and as one whose messages must land (ST-SUP-RP01-LC14, ST-SUP-RC18-OC27), which calls RunConsumer with the claimed message and the tenant, staging principal and stager that its row stores (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16), and MUST NOT register that destination for a component or another worker. A run whose fill returns an error or panics MUST make the handler return a transient refusal, not acted, because its local transaction rolled back with every write and effect, so the outbox moves the message back to pending (ST-SUP-RP01-LC09), never to outcome unknown, and never drops it. A run whose fill is denied as the staging principal, or returns a declared refusal, MUST make the handler return a permanent refusal, so the message is parked (ST-SUP-RP10-LC26). Decision of 2026-11-09 under the Product owner's delegation, on the review of PR #156.

title: Each tenant's run has its own deadline
statement: Each tenant's transaction in a tick MUST run under a deadline of its own, the earliest of 30 s after it starts, the time the next tick is due, the deadline that ST-SUP-RP10-LC22 gives under a lease and the start of shutdown, and each consumed message under a deadline of 30 s or the start of shutdown, so one slow tenant cannot use the time of the others.

title: A failed run stays in its run
statement: A worker fill that returns an error or panics MUST end only its own run with a rollback (ST-SUP-RP10-LC12), MUST NOT stop its runner, another worker or the process, and the next tick or delivery MUST run as usual.

title: Each run reports a fixed outcome
statement: The runner MUST report each run as one span named worker <worker name> of the telemetry runtime, with the attribute stego.outcome set to committed, rolled_back, fenced or panicked and no error text, and each run that does not commit as the built-in service event worker.run.failed of the probe runtime (ST-SUP-RP12-LC21), with the worker name and that outcome as its only fields.

title: Shutdown drains the runs and rolls back the rest
statement: At shutdown the runners MUST start no new run, MUST wait for the running ones up to the drain bound of the worker mode (ST-SUP-RP09-LC06), and MUST then roll back each run that is still running.

title: Each runner is started and stopped once
statement: The generated code MUST start, stop and clean up each worker's runner itself, exactly once for each process, whatever the number of stop and close calls, and no hand-written code MUST start, stop or own a runner.

title: Each tick starts from the next tenant, and the tenants it does not reach are counted
statement: A tick MUST visit the tenants in the order of the tenant list, starting with the first tenant that the previous tick did not reach, or after the last one it reached when it reached all, and a tick that ends because the next tick is due, the lease is lost or the shutdown starts MUST count each tenant that it did not reach as the built-in counter worker.tenant.unreached (ST-SUP-RP12-LC21).

title: Each worker's own tuple is written for each tenant when it is provisioned
statement: When the declaration binds authorization, the generated code MUST register a provisioning hook (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07) that stages, through the authz destination in the transaction that provisions a tenant, one tuple tenant:<tenant id>#worker_<worker name in snake case>@service_account:<worker name> for each declared worker, each on the worker's own relation so no worker holds another's permission, and one delete of each when the tenant is retired; it MUST write no tuple with a wildcard subject or resource and no tuple of another tenant. Generation MUST refuse a schema whose type tenant has no relation worker_<name> of the subject type service_account for each declared worker, and the conformance tests of ST-SUP-RC29-OC14 MUST assert, for each worker's permission, an allow for that worker's service account in its tenant and a deny for another worker's service account and for the same account in another tenant.

title: Each partner destination is one outbox destination, idempotent only when the partner accepts the key
statement: For each destination of its setting destinations (a name, an https origin, a path, a method, must_land and idempotent as ST-SUP-RC32-OC12 states, whether the partner accepts an Idempotency-Key, an optional status path with a settle time, a timeout and a credential name), the code this component emits MUST register one destination handler on the service's outbox with that name (ST-SUP-RP01-LC14), with the must_land and idempotent that the destination declares, and MUST NOT derive idempotent itself; checking MUST refuse a destination declared idempotent whose partner does not accept an Idempotency-Key, naming the destination. The orchestrator decided under the owner's delegation (2026-11-11) that the declaration states idempotent for every destination (ST-SUP-RC32-OC12).

title: A status lookup answers not acted only when the partner echoes the key
statement: When a destination declares a status path, the emitted code MUST register it as the destination's status lookup with the declared settle time, which MUST be positive (ST-SUP-RP01-LC14). The lookup MUST send GET to that path on the same origin with no body and the header Idempotency-Key that ST-SUP-RC36-OC09 states, and MUST answer acted only for a 200 answer of type application/json, at most 4 KiB, that is the object {"idempotency_key": <the same key>, "state": "acted"}, not acted only for the same object with the state not_acted, and unknown for every other answer, 404 included, a key that differs and a failure (ST-SUP-RP01-LC11). A destination with no status path MUST register no lookup.

title: A partner is reached only over verified TLS
statement: Generation MUST refuse a destination whose origin is not an https URL with a host and no path, query, user information or fragment, and each request MUST use the bounded HTTPS client that this component renders from the shared template (ST-SUP-RC10-G02), so it keeps verified TLS 1.3, one origin, no redirect, no environment proxy and the body limits (ST-SUP-RC10-OC01, ST-SUP-RC10-OC02); no plain HTTP path exists.

title: Each request has a bounded timeout
statement: Each request MUST run under the destination's timeout, from 1s to 30s and 10s when it is omitted, and generation MUST refuse any other timeout; a timeout or a lost connection after the request was written MUST end the attempt in outcome unknown (ST-SUP-RP01-LC09), and a failure before any byte was written MUST be marked as not sent.

title: The partner's response body is never stored or logged
statement: The handler MUST read at most 64 KiB of a response body and discard it, MUST decide only from the status code, and the status lookup only from the two members that ST-SUP-RC36-OC02 names; neither MUST store any part of a body, the response headers or the partner's error text in the queue, a span, a log, a probe event or an alert (ST-SUP-RP01-LC06), and neither MUST put the request payload in any of them.

title: The credential comes from the secret store on each request, never from the declaration
statement: The destination's credential MUST be a name. The emitted code MUST resolve it through the environment setting STEGO_DESTINATION_<NAME>_CREDENTIAL_FILE, where <NAME> is the destination name in upper case with each hyphen as an underscore, to a file that the environment mounts from its secret store, and MUST read that file again, at most 8 KiB and under the private credential file rule (ST-SUP-RC10-OC06), for each request and each lookup, so a rotated credential is used without a restart, and send it as a bearer token. A request whose file is missing or not private MUST NOT be sent and MUST be marked as a transient refusal; the service MUST NOT start when the file is missing or not private at start. The configuration MUST have no field for a credential value, and generation MUST refuse a destination with an inline token.

title: A partner's answer moves the message only through the dispatch states
statement: The handler MUST return success for a 2xx answer; a transient refusal for 408, 425, 429, 502, 503 and 504, and for 409 when the destination is idempotent; a permanent refusal for every other 4xx answer, 409 at a destination that is not idempotent included, and for a 3xx answer; and an error that it does not mark for 500 and every other answer, so the outbox moves the message only as ST-SUP-RP01-LC08 to ST-SUP-RP01-LC12 state; the handler MUST NOT retry, wait or call the partner a second time itself.

title: A fake partner is emitted for local tests
statement: The generator MUST emit, in a test package, a fake partner for each destination: an in-process TLS server with a test CA, which records each request with its headers and body, answers each request with a status that the test sets, can hold or drop a request and can serve the status lookup, and a constructor that points the destination at it, so a service's tests and fill tests run with no network and no outside system.

title: Every request and every lookup carry the derived key in the Idempotency-Key header
statement: Each request and each status lookup MUST carry the header Idempotency-Key whose value is the message's stored outgoing key (ST-SUP-RP01-LC10), as the 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06), the same on every attempt, whether the destination is idempotent or not; only at an idempotent destination does the outbox rely on the partner to act once for one key and send again after an unknown outcome.

title: The request body is the effect payload as JSON
statement: Each request MUST use the destination's method, POST when it is omitted, MUST have the header Content-Type: application/json and MUST have as its body the effect's payload as canonical JSON in the form of ST-SUP-RP07-LC05 (sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace, one form for numbers), with no other member and no envelope.

title: Any provider is found by its issuer
statement: The verifier this component emits MUST verify the tokens of any OpenID Connect provider that the declaration names by its issuer URL, MUST find the provider's key set through its discovery document at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration, fetched over verified TLS, and MUST refuse a discovery document whose issuer is not the declared issuer or whose key set URL is not an HTTPS URL. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider; the new component and rh-sso-auth as its configuration are the orchestrator's design under the owner's delegation. The declared issuer MUST pass the check of the runtime verifier at generation: an HTTPS URL with a host, no user, query or fragment, and the same text after TrimSpace. The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation, after the security review of PR #202.

title: The declared audience and the accepted algorithms only
statement: The verifier this component emits MUST accept only a token for the declared audience, signed with one of the declared accepted signing algorithms, each of them in the allow list of the runtime verifier (ST-SUP-RP13-LC03), and MUST refuse every other token. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider; the new component and rh-sso-auth as its configuration are the orchestrator's design under the owner's delegation. The declared audience MUST be the audience of the API, not the client ID of the application that signs in, and the verifier MUST refuse an ID token (ST-SUP-RP13-LC03). The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation, after the security review of PR #202.

title: The subject and the tenant come from the declared claims
statement: The verifier this component emits MUST map the subject and the tenant claim that the declaration names, and MUST refuse a token that does not hold them. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider; the new component and rh-sso-auth as its configuration are the orchestrator's design under the owner's delegation. The declared subject claim MUST be sub, the default, or oid, and the generator MUST refuse every other subject claim, such as email, preferred_username or upn (ST-SUP-RP13-LC13). The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-11 under the Product owner's delegation, after the security review of PR #202.

title: The runtime verifier does the verification
statement: This component MUST verify through the verifier of the runtime library (ST-SUP-RP13) and MUST emit no verifier, key set or key source of its own; a helper that the runtime does not give yet is a runtime change. The Product owner decided on 2026-11-11 that sign-in on the runtime data path supports any OpenID Connect provider; the new component and rh-sso-auth as its configuration are the orchestrator's design under the owner's delegation.
